result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly explain why the form looks like a blob and give concrete CSS with a tight label-to-input gap and a wider gap between fields. B does better on grouping: it splits the form into three fieldsets (about you, riding, emergency contact) with 32px between groups and 20px between fields, so there are three clear spacing levels. A only wraps the emergency contact in a fieldset, and that group still sits 24px from the field above it, the same as any two fields, so its larger gap (40px) is only an optional suggestion. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain the uniform-spacing problem well and set a tight label-to-input gap with a larger gap between fields. A also groups all three related sets (about you, riding, emergency) with a clearly bigger 32px gap between groups and extra room above the button. B groups only the emergency contact, and in its flex layout the gap between groups is the same 24px as between fields, so the group hierarchy is weaker.
